Scenario: Pedestrian on or stepping onto a marked crosswalk
Description: The vehicle approaches a marked crosswalk in lane while a pedestrian is on it or steps onto it
ODD attributes varied (WP-C-02): ODD-20, ODD-03, ODD-05, ODD-16, ODD-12, ODD-10, ODD-13
Pass criterion: No contact with the pedestrian; the vehicle yields as the traffic rules require, and the monitor commands the deceleration that restores the safe distance whenever Autoware does not; unjustified hard braking counts against the SOTIF acceptance criteria

Scenario: Pedestrian emerging from behind a parked vehicle
Description: A pedestrian, child or cyclist steps out from behind a parked van or bus away from a crossing, where pedestrians are dense
Pass criterion: The vehicle's speed near the occlusion lets it stop for a road user emerging at the assumed speed; no contact, and no swerve out of the drivable area to avoid one

Scenario: Vehicle ahead braking or stopping in congested traffic
Description: The vehicle follows another in congestion or in free flow; the lead vehicle brakes hard, stops, or another vehicle cuts in
ODD attributes varied (WP-C-02): ODD-20, ODD-03, ODD-17, ODD-16, ODD-13, ODD-10
Pass criterion: No collision with the vehicle ahead; acceleration stays inside the envelope, the monitor restores the safe longitudinal distance, and a braking shortfall on a wet road switches to the secondary path

Scenario: Spurious obstacle with a road user following
Description: Spray, steam, blowing debris or a soiled sensor produces a false obstacle in the path while a car or motorcycle follows closely, possibly with an unbelted passenger
Pass criterion: Braking that the safety channel does not confirm stays at or below the firm level; emergency braking happens only when a road user is confirmed; a blocked safety sensor is detected and Autoware stops comfortably; the belt warning acts

Scenario: Signalised intersection with cross traffic
Description: The vehicle approaches a signalised intersection; the signal is hard to read, dark or meant for another lane, or a crossing vehicle runs its red
Pass criterion: The vehicle enters only on a recognised green and treats an unknown signal as red; whatever the signal, it does not enter when its swept path crosses that of a detected road user before it could stop or clear

Scenario: Unprotected left turn across oncoming traffic
Description: Left turn on a permissive green or at an uncontrolled junction, with an oncoming lane hidden by a turning vehicle, or a motorcycle approaching fast
Pass criterion: The vehicle starts the turn only with a gap that lets the oncoming road user pass at its assumed speed and acceleration, and stops before the conflict area otherwise

Scenario: Entry to a roundabout with traffic circulating
Description: The vehicle enters a single-lane or multi-lane roundabout while vehicles circulate
Pass criterion: The vehicle yields to circulating traffic and enters only with a gap that its assumed speed allows

Scenario: Cyclist alongside on the inside of a turn
Description: A cyclist or scooter rider rides up on the inside as the vehicle turns, or swerves between lanes round an obstacle
Pass criterion: No steering command whose swept path comes within the safe lateral distance of the cyclist is executed; the vehicle waits or stops in lane

Scenario: Lane keeping where localisation is degraded
Description: Driving in lane beside oncoming traffic or the sidewalk on a street with few features, many moved objects, or large vehicles blocking the view
ODD attributes varied (WP-C-02): ODD-20, ODD-01, ODD-02, ODD-03, ODD-07, ODD-08, ODD-15, ODD-17, ODD-06
Pass criterion: The vehicle stays in its lane and drivable area; a steering command toward a detected road user or kerb is rejected and the vehicle stops in lane; a degraded pose is detected

Scenario: Work zone or re-marked lanes not yet in the map
Description: The road ahead has been re-marked, closed or turned into a work zone that the HD map does not show
Pass criterion: The divergence monitor detects the disagreement and the vehicle carries out a minimal risk manoeuvre; it never follows the map into a closed lane

Scenario: Person directing traffic
Description: A police officer, flagger or first responder directs traffic at a junction or a scene
Pass criterion: The vehicle detects the person directing traffic, stops safely and asks for remote assistance; it does not move on the signal alone, and responders can stop or hold it

Scenario: Emergency vehicle approaching with siren and lights
Description: An emergency vehicle approaches from behind, ahead or across a junction while the vehicle drives or waits
Pass criterion: The vehicle detects the emergency vehicle, pulls to the side when safe or stops, and lets it pass; when it cannot yield it reaches a minimal risk condition

Scenario: Rare object or debris in the lane
Description: A fallen load, low debris, an animal, an e-scooter lying in the lane, or cones placed to trap the vehicle
Pass criterion: The vehicle stops before the object or passes it within the lane when clear; a vehicle that cannot find a way on reaches a minimal risk condition and asks for help

Scenario: Weather changing toward the ODD limits during a trip
Description: Rain grows heavier or visibility falls during a trip, up to and past the limits of the ODD
ODD attributes varied (WP-C-02): ODD-20, ODD-10, ODD-11, ODD-12, ODD-13, ODD-16
Pass criterion: The weather monitor detects the exit, treats a reading it cannot tell from the limit as outside, and the vehicle reaches a minimal risk condition; detection inside the ODD still meets the safety channel's requirement

Scenario: Kerbside stop while passengers board or alight
Description: The vehicle pulls in to a mapped stop, passengers get in and out, including slowly or with help, and the vehicle pulls out; a person may stand behind it
Pass criterion: The vehicle does not move with a door open or a person in the near field in the direction of travel, never reverses, and resumes only when every release condition holds

Scenario: Stopped at a red light with pedestrians crossing in front
Description: The vehicle waits at a red light or in a queue on a gradient while pedestrians cross in front of it
Pass criterion: The vehicle stays held until every release condition holds; motion while holding is detected and the park brake applied; no acceleration toward a detected road user

Scenario: Loss of Autoware while driving
Description: Autoware's commands stop, freeze or become implausible while driving in lane; other road users then pass the vehicle stopped in lane
Pass criterion: The monitor detects the loss within its detection budget and stops the vehicle in lane with hazard lights on, without Autoware; a fault of the monitor itself leads to the vehicle's own stop, never to the park brake while moving

Scenario: Pull-over minimal risk manoeuvre along a busy kerb
Description: Autoware pulls over after a stop request or a minor fault, where the kerb has bike lanes, driveways, bus stops or crosswalks
Pass criterion: The vehicle pulls over only into a mapped safe stopping place and stops in lane otherwise; repeated stop requests go to a remote operator

Scenario: Passengers leaving at a stop in lane
Description: After a minimal risk manoeuvre the vehicle stands in a traffic lane and passengers open the doors on the traffic side
Pass criterion: The vehicle holds the minimal risk condition with hazard lights on and warns passengers of traffic on their side before they leave; the residual risk counts against the SOTIF acceptance criteria

Scenario: Remote driving with a delayed or lost link
Description: A remote operator drives the vehicle at walking pace; video and commands are delayed, compressed or lost, or the operator is tired or busy
Pass criterion: Commands older than the age bound, out of sequence or failing their integrity check are rejected and the vehicle stops; the envelope checks apply to remote commands as to Autoware's; a remote emergency stop brakes firmly unless the safety channel confirms a road user

Scenario: Remote release of the wrong vehicle or at the wrong moment
Description: A remote operator releases or moves a vehicle that is not the one meant, or a release message is replayed
Pass criterion: A release moves the vehicle only when it is bound to that vehicle, authentic and fresh, and the release conditions hold

Scenario: Turn indicator during a turn or lane change
Description: The vehicle changes lane to pass a stopped vehicle, or turns at a junction, with other road users relying on its indicator
Pass criterion: The indicator always matches the commanded and achieved steering direction; on a mismatch hazard lights come on

Scenario: Give and take with other drivers
Description: Four-way stops, merging and letting another vehicle out, where other drivers expect the vehicle to negotiate
Pass criterion: The vehicle takes its turn as the rules give it and shows when it yields and when it is about to move; its hesitations and stops count against the SOTIF acceptance criteria

Scenario: Passenger misuse and emergencies in the cabin
Description: A passenger tries to take control, a passenger has a medical emergency or is threatened, or a child rides alone or is left behind
Pass criterion: No control is reachable from the cabin; every seat reaches a remote operator who can divert the vehicle; no trip ends with a person inside without an operator's decision

Scenario: First responders at a collision
Description: After a collision the vehicle stops; responders need to make it safe, open the doors and move it
Pass criterion: The vehicle stops and holds after a collision; doors open from inside without power; responders can find the isolation points and reach remote operations

Scenario: Return to service after maintenance
Description: A technician returns a vehicle with a misaligned or dirty sensor, mixed software versions, or parameters changed through a service port
Pass criterion: The vehicle refuses driverless dispatch until calibration, cleanliness and versions are checked and recorded; parameter changes outside the release process are rejected
